findings.issue_text: [BUG] The new destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` crashes with a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, because the code no longer uses optional chaining before accessing .integration. Any booking without a destination calendar (the common case for users with no calendar app connected) that selects Cal Video as location throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` inside EventManager, failing the entire booking flow with a 500 instead of falling back to daily video as the previous code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) did.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback branch `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares each calendar's externalId against undefined and always returns undefined — the condition is tautological and the previous fallback to `destinationCalendar.externalId` is destroyed. Reschedules/updates of a Google calendar event that rely on the booking's stored destinationCalendar (no externalCalendarId argument) now pass `calendarId: undefined` to calendar.events.update, which makes the Google API reject the call and the calendar update silently fails; the same tautological find at lines 312-315 breaks deleteEvent the same way.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent keeps its single-event signature and always picks `event.destinationCalendar[0]` (the 'main host' calendar), ignoring the credentialId parameter that the new Calendar interface passes in, so every O365 host in a collective booking creates the event on the first host's calendar. For a collective booking with multiple Office365 hosts, each host's credential call writes the event to host #1's calendar instead of each host's own destination calendar — the multiple-calendar behavior this PR is supposed to deliver does not work for O365 at all, and the same unfiltered 'first element' assumption recurs in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 156-160 and larkcalendar CalendarService.ts lines 128-129.

[BUG] The booking create statement connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` to the booking's (singular) destinationCalendar relation, so the additional teamDestinationCalendars pushed for collective events are never persisted on the booking. On reschedule or cancellation, handleCancelBooking/EventManager rebuild the calendar list from booking.destinationCalendar, which contains only the first host's calendar — the other collective hosts' calendar events are orphaned (never updated or deleted) even though createAllCalendarEvents created one event per host calendar.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when destinationCalendar is null (the case when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one), and the preceding teamMemberPromises loop reads `user.destinationCalendar` from user objects whose select (dynamic-user prisma select / eventType.users) is not shown to include the destinationCalendar relation. For collective events where the organizer has no destination calendar, all team members' destination calendars are silently dropped instead of being used, so no per-host calendar events are created; if the user query select lacks destinationCalendar the push list is empty for every collective booking regardless.

[ADVISORY] The DB-fallback credential fetch requires `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` to be truthy, but core calendar credentials (e.g. google_calendar credentials created before the App Store migration, or credentials whose App row is absent) have no related App record, so the constructed credential stays undefined and the destination is silently skipped. Legacy/pre-App-Store credentials referenced by a destinationCalendar.credentialId cause that host's calendar event to be silently not created (no error surfaced), reproducing exactly the class of silent-skip bug this refactor was meant to fix; the same copy-pasted fallback in updateAllCalendarEvents (lines ~505-520) and the one in handleCancelBooking has the same dependency.

[ADVISORY] createEvent now receives `externalId` as a parameter but never uses it inside the function body — it is only echoed back in the EventResult, so the parameter is dead except as a passthrough. The next reader assumes externalId influences calendar selection (as the Google service's own credentialId-based lookup does) and builds on a parameter that has no effect, increasing confusion in an already tangled selection path; deletion of the parameter from the signature would be behavior-neutral.

[ADVISORY] teamDestinationCalendars is populated via side effect inside a `.map()` callback (teamMemberPromises), so calendar collection is an accidental byproduct of attendee translation with hidden ordering/coupling. Any future change that reorders, filters, or short-circuits the teamMemberPromises map (e.g. skipping users without locale) silently changes which destination calendars get booked against; a dedicated collection step before the map would make the coupling explicit and removable.

[BUG] The Meet-location fallback dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without a null guard, crashing when destinationCalendar is null/empty (the old code used optional chaining). When evt.destinationCalendar is null (no calendar connected, the common single-user case) and location is Google Meet, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws TypeError, failing the booking with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video as the contract promises.

[BUG] deleteEvent's new find is inverted: when externalCalendarId is falsy, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === undefined)` never matches, so the destinationCalendar fallback that the old code used is dropped and the delete targets primary. Cancelling a booking that has a destinationCalendar but no persisted externalCalendarId on the reference deletes the event from the organizer's primary calendar (or fails with 404/410 on the wrong calendar), leaving the real calendar event orphaned.

[BUG] updateEvent's `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is a tautology when externalCalendarId is truthy and returns undefined when it is falsy, removing the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. Updating a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now passes calendarId undefined to calendar.events.update instead of the destination calendar id, so the update hits the wrong calendar or errors.

[BUG] For COLLECTIVE events, teamDestinationCalendars is populated only from users.slice(1), so the destinationCalendar of users[0] is never added unless users[0] happens to be organizerUser. A collective event whose first listed host is not the booking organizer silently books only into the organizer's calendar plus hosts 2..n, dropping the first host's calendar — directly contradicting the PR's 'collective multiple host on destinationCalendar' requirement.

[BUG] Office365 createEvent ignores the per-credential selection and always uses the first destinationCalendar element, so with the new multi-destination array both hosts' events are created in the first host's calendar. For a collective booking with two O365 hosts, createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per credential, but both calls read destinationCalendar[0], writing the second host's event into the first host's calendar (same defect in larkcalendar createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent and BaseCalendarService at packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156).

[ADVISORY] Reschedule merging still deletes only the first old calendar reference (`booking.references.find`) even though references are now expected to be multiple. Cancelling/rescheduling a collective booking created by this PR leaves the non-first hosts' old calendar events orphaned on their calendars, since only one old event is deleted while createAllCalendarEvents created one per host.

[ADVISORY] No test in this diff exercises the new multi-destination behavior: the only test touched is a webhook payload assertion (destinationCalendar: []), while createAllCalendarEvents, credential-from-DB fallback, Google per-credential find, and the collective teamDestinationCalendars accumulation have zero coverage. A regression in any of the new loops or the credential lookup (e.g., the DB-fetch fallback building an invalid credential object) ships silently; the changed webhook snapshot does not verify that multiple destinations are actually created or referenced.

[ADVISORY] paypal-webhook wraps the result in an array while the sibling stripe webhook (webhook.ts) uses `[]` for the empty case — inconsistent normalization across the payment paths the diff touched. Downstream consumers of evt.destinationCalendar must handle both null-adjacent shapes; the next call site converted to array semantics (e.g., EventManager's `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` non-guarded access) will crash on whichever shape its author didn't test.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback lookup was rewritten to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which searches for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId even in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy/undefined, so it always yields undefined. When updateEvent is called without externalCalendarId (e.g. reschedule flows that rely on destinationCalendar), calendarId becomes undefined instead of the previously-used destinationCalendar.externalId, so the update targets a wrong/undefined calendar and the event update fails or hits the wrong calendar.

[BUG] Same pattern in deleteEvent: the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs the find with a falsy externalCalendarId, so it can never match and returns undefined. Deleting a booking that relied on destinationCalendar falls back to calendarId 'primary', deleting/mismatching the wrong calendar event instead of the originally booked calendar.

[BUG] The booking create payload connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` while the collective feature pushes multiple destinationCalendars onto evt, so only the first member's calendar is persisted as the booking's destinationCalendar reference. The other collective members' calendar events are created but never linked as booking references; subsequent reschedule/cancel flows that iterate booking references (which this same diff now does) will only see one reference, leaving orphaned events on the other members' calendars on cancellation.

[BUG] Every calendar service now treats destinationCalendar[0] as 'the main host' calendar, but with the collective multi-calendar array the first element can belong to a different integration or a different member than the service instance being executed. Google/Lark/O365 services use another member's or another integration's externalId as the organizer attendee email, producing events with a wrong organizer identity on the created calendar events.

[ADVISORY] createEvent now takes both an externalId parameter and returns credentialId/externalId, but Google's createEvent ignores the externalId argument and re-derives the calendar by matching credentialId against destinationCalendar — two parallel sources of truth for the same fact. The next contributor must keep the credentialId-based lookup in GoogleCalendarService and the externalId threading through CalendarManager in sync; if a credential owns multiple calendars the two mechanisms disagree silently.

[ADVISORY] The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but only GoogleCalendarService was updated; Lark and Office365 createEvent implementations still declare only (event). TypeScript method bivariance lets this compile, but the contract change is half-applied: a strict-mode or contravariant tightening, or any new service author copying the interface, will pass credentialId that Lark/O365 silently ignore — the multiple-destination fix only works for Google.

[ADVISORY] `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType` is added to the CalendarEvent payload and a SchedulingType field added to the CalendarEvent interface, but no code in this diff ever reads evt.schedulingType. Ships-inert API surface: a payload field crossing into every calendar/email path with no consumer, inviting future readers to assume it drives behavior it does not; the isTeamEventType && COLLECTIVE check is done inline at push time instead.

[ADVISORY] Rewriting `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to a ternary and the metadata spread in organizations create.handler has no traceable connection to the collective multi-destination-calendar fix. Scope drift: an unrelated org-creation code change rides in a calendar fix, muddying review and revert ability if the calendar change needs to be rolled back independently.

[ADVISORY] loadUsers is rewritten wholesale — new try/catch with generic 500 'Unable to load users', an added dynamicUserList empty guard that throws, and removal of the `organization` select from the dynamic-user prisma query — none of which is required by the destinationCalendar change. Scope drift plus behavior change: dynamic-booking users now load without organization data (any downstream consumer of user.organization silently gets undefined), and previously-warned paths now throw 500s; all untraceable to the PR's stated intent.

[ADVISORY] isTeamEventType is rewritten from an enum comparison to a string-array includes, and the orginalBookingDuration→originalBookingDuration rename are drive-by refactors unrelated to the destination calendar work. Behaviorally equivalent but unreviewable diff noise in a security-sensitive booking path; it expands the blast radius of this PR beyond the stated fix.

[ADVISORY] The credential-from-DB fallback block (prisma.credential.findUnique with app include, manual object assembly) is duplicated verbatim in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents and EventManager.updateCalendarReferences, and a third near-copy appears in handleCancelBooking.ts. Three hand-maintained copies of the credential-rehydration logic must stay in sync with the Credential shape (appName/id/type/key/userId/teamId/invalid/appId); the next Credential field addition silently diverges in whichever copy is missed, and one copy (handleCancelBooking) already omits the app.slug guard the others have.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback dereferences the first element of destinationCalendar without checking it exists: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"`. Any booking with destinationCalendar null (the new default when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one, per handleNewBooking.ts line ~1064) or an empty array throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` during event creation, instead of falling back to Cal Video as before.

[BUG] In updateEvent, the fallback lookup `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares each calendar's externalId against undefined and never matches. When no explicit externalCalendarId is passed (the common path, since old booking references and the new no-credentialId path store none), selectedCalendar is undefined and the update is issued against Google's default 'primary' calendar instead of the calendar the event actually lives in, leaving the real event stale/never updated.

[BUG] In deleteEvent, the same tautological lookup `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always returns undefined and calendarId falls back to 'primary'. Cancellations delete a (possibly nonexistent) event from the user's primary calendar while the original event in the actual destination calendar is never deleted — orphaned calendar events persist on every cancelled booking that has no externalCalendarId reference.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null, silently dropping all collective hosts' destination calendars in exactly the case where neither the eventType nor the organizer has one but team members do. For COLLECTIVE bookings whose eventType and organizer have no destinationCalendar, team members' calendars are never created-in, contradicting the PR's stated purpose of handling collective multiple hosts; the booking silently books only on... nothing.

[BUG] The non-isCalendarType result mapping changed `externalCalendarId: evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, but result.externalId is only populated by CalendarManager.createEvent for calendar credentials — video/conferencing results never have it, and the no-credentialId createEvent call in createAllCalendarEvents passes no externalId so it is undefined there too. BookingReferences that previously recorded the destination calendar's externalId now record undefined; downstream update/delete flows then hit the broken find-by-undefined lookups in GoogleCalendarService and operate on 'primary', a sentinel-meaning change with no caller adaptation.

[BUG] In the no-credentialId destination branch, createEvent is called as `createEvent(c, event)` without destination.externalId, so GoogleCalendarService.createEvent's `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` cannot match (the destination has no credentialId by definition of this branch) and falls back to 'primary'. Legacy bookings created before the refactor whose DestinationCalendar rows have no credentialId but do have a specific externalId now get their events created on the user's primary calendar instead of the selected calendar — a silent regression for pre-existing data.

[ADVISORY] The inline 'fetch credential from DB and reshape it' block is duplicated verbatim between createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents (and a third variant exists in handleCancelBooking.ts), a parallel hand-maintained enumeration of the Credential shape. The next field added to Credential (or changed in the prisma select) must be updated in three scattered inline object literals; one will be missed and a half-populated credential will be passed to calendar services at runtime.

[ADVISORY] The per-destination loop issues a `prisma.credential.findUnique` per destination inside the iteration (N+1), and handleCancelBooking.ts repeats the same per-reference DB fetch inside its loop. A collective booking with many hosts (or a cancellation touching many references) issues one sequential DB round-trip per destination instead of one batched `findMany({ id: { in: [...] } })`, adding latency to the booking hot path linear in host count.

[ADVISORY] The Booking write still connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` because the schema keeps a single one-to-one Booking→DestinationCalendar relation, so the multi-calendar model exists only in the in-memory CalendarEvent and is not persisted as the source of truth. Every later flow that rebuilds the CalendarEvent from `booking.destinationCalendar` (confirm.handler, editLocation, paypal/stripe webhooks, bookingReminder cron — all wrapped as `[booking.destinationCalendar]` in this diff) sees only the first host's calendar; the collective multi-host state is unrepresentable in the data model and is silently lost after creation.

[ADVISORY] `teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar)` pushes null entries when a collective host has no destinationCalendar, and the array is later spread into evt.destinationCalendar. A null entry can become element 0 of evt.destinationCalendar (e.g. organizer has none so the base is null... skipped, or is ordered first via users.slice), at which point `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...` yields null and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in EventManager crashes the same way as the undefined case.

[ADVISORY] The Calendar interface's createEvent signature was changed to require `credentialId: number`, but only GoogleCalendarService's implementation was updated — Lark, Office365, and BaseCalendarService implementations still declare/create `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` while EventManager now calls with two arguments. The interface and its implementers disagree; any strictly-typed implementation or new calendar app written against the interface compiles expecting one argument and never receives the credentialId it needs to disambiguate destination calendars, repeating the very mismatch this PR fixes for Google only.

[ADVISORY] `credential` is declared once outside the reference loop and never reset between iterations, so a stale credential from a previous iteration leaks into later iterations' `updateEvent(credential, ...)` when a lookup fails silently. If iteration 1 resolves a credential and iteration 2's reference has a credentialId that matches nothing (DB fetch also fails), `credential` still holds iteration 1's value and the update is issued against the wrong host's calendar with the wrong auth.

[ADVISORY] `isTeamEventType` was rewritten from the imported SchedulingType enum constants to magic string literals `["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`, abandoning the typed enum used one line later (`eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`). A rename or new scheduling type in the Prisma enum no longer fails compilation here; the stringly-typed discriminator drifts from `SchedulingType` imported elsewhere in the same file.

[BUG] The spread conditions were silently inverted: the old code set slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false and requestedSlug when it is true, the new code sets slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true and requestedSlug when it is false. With team billing disabled, organizations are created without a slug (breaking org URL resolution) and with no requestedSlug; with billing enabled, both slug and requestedSlug get set, changing the onboarding flow — an objective reversal snuck in under a refactoring commit with no test or human acceptance.

[BUG] The null-safe access evt.destinationCalendar?.integration was replaced with an unconditional member access on a destructured element, so mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. Every booking whose CalendarEvent has no destinationCalendar (the evt is built with destinationCalendar: null in handleNewBooking when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one) now crashes with a TypeError inside EventManager instead of skipping the Google Meet fallback check — a regression on the previously-working no-calendar path.

[BUG] createEvent dropped the destinationCalendar.externalId fallback and now only matches a destination whose credentialId equals this credential's id, otherwise silently creating the event on 'primary'. When destinationCalendar carries an externalId but its credentialId doesn't match the invoking credential (the exact 404 mismatch scenario the old code handled), the event is silently written to the organizer's primary calendar instead of the user-selected destination calendar — bookings land on the wrong calendar with no error.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback changed from event.destinationCalendar?.externalId to event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId, which when externalCalendarId is falsy searches for calendars whose externalId equals undefined. Any updateEvent call without an externalCalendarId now resolves selectedCalendar to undefined, so calendar.events.update is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the Google API call fails — previously the update targeted the destination calendar's externalId and succeeded.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same regression: the fallback now searches for externalId === externalCalendarId (undefined when not passed) instead of using event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. Deleting a booking without an explicit externalCalendarId resolves calendarId to undefined and the delete fails, leaving orphaned calendar events for bookings whose references lack externalCalendarId — the exact case the old fallback covered.

[BUG] For COLLECTIVE team events, team member destination calendars are only pushed when evt.destinationCalendar is already non-null, and the booking row only connects destinationCalendar[0]. When neither the eventType nor the organizer has a destination calendar but team members do (evt.destinationCalendar is null), the push is silently skipped by optional chaining and collective bookings create no calendar events for members who configured calendars — the PR's stated intent (collective multiple-host destination calendars) silently does not apply in that case, without any accepted decision to exclude it.

[BUG] loadUsers dropped the organization: { select: { slug: true } } select from the dynamic-user prisma.user.findMany while keeping the same downstream consumers of the loaded users. Any downstream logic in handleNewBooking that reads user.organization.slug (e.g. org-scoped handling of dynamically listed users) now sees undefined, changing behavior for dynamic collective bookings on organizations without an explicit review of that data dependency.

[ADVISORY] The old code fell back to bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar (a duplicated operand, almost certainly intended to fall back to the user's destinationCalendar); the new code drops the fallback arm entirely rather than fixing it to user.destinationCalendar. A pre-existing bug is silently removed along with its intended fallback semantics; reschedule-request emails/updates for bookings without a booking-level destinationCalendar now run with an empty array where the author evidently meant to fall back to the user's calendar — the fix changed the objective (bug cleanup) without flagging it for review.

[ADVISORY] The isTeamEventType definition was rewritten from an explicit SchedulingType enum comparison to a string-array includes check on raw schedulingType values. Behavior is equivalent today, but the string literals 'COLLECTIVE'/'ROUND_ROBIN' bypass the enum as single source of truth: a rename or new scheduling type will fail silently at this string comparison instead of at compile time, and the same string literal is duplicated again in the teamDestinationCalendars push below — the next change to scheduling types gets riskier.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated copy change (organiser → organizer in the hideCalendarNotes string) was slipped into the same commit as the destinationCalendar array refactor. User-visible email text changes are bundled invisibly with a schema-shape refactor; reviewers accepting 'collective destination calendar support' also silently accepted a copy change nobody signed off on — textbook intent drift inside an iteration.

[BUG] createAllCalendarEvents fetches a credential from the database by destination.credentialId with no userId/teamId scope check, so any credential id referenced by a destinationCalendar row is loaded with its full secret key. If any code path lets a destinationCalendar reference a credential the booking owner does not own (e.g. imported booking data, collective members' calendars pointing at another user's credential, or future client-supplied calendar selection), the organizer's OAuth key is used to write events into another user's calendar — cross-tenant calendar write. The lookup WHERE id=$credentialId has no userId filter, unlike this.calendarCredentials which is pre-scoped to the booking's users.

[BUG] updateAllCalendarEvents performs the same unscoped prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } }) with no ownership scoping on the fetched credential. Same cross-tenant exposure as the create path: an unscoped reference.credentialId causes the fetched credential's secret key to be used to update/delete events on a calendar the booking owner may not control; the query trusts the id with no userId or teamId filter.

[BUG] handleCancelBooking fetches prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) with no userId/teamId scope when the reference's credentialId is not among the booking user's credentials. A booking reference carrying a credentialId owned by a different user results in that foreign credential (including its secret key via getCalendar) being used to delete events on the other user's calendar; the fallback lookup deliberately bypasses the ownership check the user.credentials.find() filter previously enforced.

[BUG] After the destinationCalendar fallback becomes an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` dereferences undefined and throws a TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is []. Any booking flow that reaches EventManager with destinationCalendar set to [] (the new normalized empty state used by handleCancelBooking, paypal-webhook, and stripe webhook) crashes with an unhandled TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video, breaking booking creation/rescheduling for users with no destination calendar.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten createAllCalendarEvents multi-destination loop, the new prisma.credential.findUnique DB fallback, and the new createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId) call have no test in this diff — the only test change is apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts line 249, which merely updates the expected serialized payload shape (destinationCalendar: []); it never exercises multiple destination calendars, the credential-from-DB fallback, or the per-credential event creation. A regression in the credential lookup loop (e.g. fetching the wrong credential or skipping a destination) would silently create calendar events on the wrong host's calendar or drop one host's event entirely, and no test in the suite would catch it because the diff's only test change pins the webhook payload shape, not the EventManager behavior.

[ADVISORY] The new credentialId-matching branch in createEvent — `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` with fallback to "primary" — has no test anywhere in the diff covering either the match path or the no-match path, even though the no-match path now silently targets "primary" instead of the previously selected calendar. When destinationCalendar entries don't carry the matching credentialId (exactly the 404 scenario the CalendarManager catch block at packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230-250 was written to tolerate), Google events are created on the organizer's primary calendar without any warning, and no test in this diff asserts which calendarId is used, so a wrong-calendar regression ships undetected.

[ADVISORY] The new COLLECTIVE teamDestinationCalendars accumulation (pushing each team member's destinationCalendar into evt.destinationCalendar) — the headline feature of this PR — is verified only by the shape-only update to apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249, which asserts `destinationCalendar: []` in a BOOKING_REJECTED payload and never asserts a multi-entry array or that the correct calendars are selected per host. A bug where team members' destinationCalendars are not pushed (e.g. the `users.slice(1)` slice omitting the only collective member, or the eventType.destinationCalendar-only path) would pass the entire test suite, since the single e2e assertion only checks empty-array serialization of an unrelated booking flow.

[BUG] The Meet-fallback check dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a null guard, so destinationCalendar === null (the common case now that handleNewBooking sets it to null) throws TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Every booking without a destination calendar that selects Google Meet crashes inside EventManager with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' where the old code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) correctly fell back to integrations:daily; booking creation 500s.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is tautological: it runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares each cal.externalId against undefined and always returns undefined, replacing the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. Reschedule/update of any booking whose stored reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the Google API rejects the update (or writes to the wrong target), so reschedules silently fail to propagate to the organizer's calendar. The same tautological find is repeated in deleteEvent (lines 312-315), so deletes without externalCalendarId now target calendarId undefined instead of the destination calendar.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when evt.destinationCalendar is null, dropping all collected teamDestinationCalendars for COLLECTIVE bookings where neither the eventType nor the organizer has a destination calendar. For collective team events with no eventType-level calendar, the other members' destination calendars are collected into teamDestinationCalendars but never attached to evt, so their calendar events are silently never created while the booking API still reports success — dropped work reported as success.

[BUG] When no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, createEvent silently falls back to calendarId "primary", creating the event on the credential's primary calendar instead of the selected destination. The 404 scenario this PR was meant to fix is now masked as a silent partial success: the event lands on the wrong calendar, the booking stores the reference anyway, and subsequent updates/deletes target the wrong calendar id — with no log and no error surfaced to the user.

[BUG] In createAllCalendarEvents, when the DB-fetched credential has no app relation (credentialFromDB.app?.slug is null), credential stays undefined and the destination is silently skipped with no log and no failure result. A booking referencing a calendar credential whose app record is missing returns success to the user while that destination calendar event is silently never created — dropped work reported as success, with zero observability.

[BUG] The spread condition was inverted: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` now always sets the organization slug, whereas the old `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set it only when billing was disabled. With team billing enabled, organizations are created with a live slug immediately at signup instead of waiting for payment, and requestedSlug is no longer reserved in metadata — unpaying users can now claim and hold org slugs, the exact behavior the billing gate existed to prevent.

[BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when neither the in-memory credentials nor the DB fetch yield a credential, `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is still invoked with credential undefined. getCalendar(undefined) throws inside the loop, which is caught by the outer catch and converted into failure results for ALL calendar references — one missing credential turns every reference's update (including ones that would have succeeded) into reported failures, and the real cause (missing credential) is misreported under the generic error message.

[ADVISORY] The reference loop multiplies remote delete calls: for each of N calendar references, the no-credentialId branch deletes via all M calendar credentials and the recurring branch loops all updatedBookings, issuing N×M (or N×bookings) deleteEvent calls against the same uids. Users with multiple calendar references on a booking now trigger duplicate remote DELETE requests to Google/Office365 on every cancellation — amplified outbound API calls that can exhaust API quotas and produce confusing 404/410 retry noise, with no dedup or bound.

[ADVISORY] createEvent swallows every non-404 error into `return undefined` with only a server log (and the broken-integration email disabled), so the caller cannot distinguish 'created' from 'failed' — and with multi-destination creation this PR adds, one failed destination is invisible in the returned EventResult shape beyond a boolean. With the new fan-out to multiple destination calendars, a partial failure (e.g., 2 of 3 calendars created) is indistinguishable from full success to callers storing booking references — the stored externalCalendarId/credentialId for the failed destination points at a nonexistent event, and later reschedules/deletes of that reference fail opaquely.

[ADVISORY] In the first result mapping, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the old fallback to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`, so when calendar creation failed (creationResult undefined), the stored booking reference has a null credentialId. When neither the eventType nor the organizer has a destination calendar but team members do (evt.destinationCalendar is null), the push is silently skipped by optional chaining and collective bookings create no calendar events for members who configured calendars — the PR's stated intent (collective multiple-host destination calendars) silently does not apply in that case, without any accepted decision to exclude it.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Downstream, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` only iterates destinations when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`, so those member events won’t be created. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] loadUsers dropped the organization: { select: { slug: true } } select from the dynamic-user prisma.user.findMany while keeping the same downstream consumers of the loaded users. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The old code fell back to bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar (a duplicated operand, almost certainly intended to fall back to the user's destinationCalendar); the new code drops the fallback arm entirely rather than fixing it to user.destinationCalendar. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createAllCalendarEvents fetches a credential from the database by destination.credentialId with no userId/teamId scope check, so any credential id referenced by a destinationCalendar row is loaded with its full secret key. If any code path lets a destinationCalendar reference a credential the booking owner does not own (e.g. imported booking data, collective members' calendars pointing at another user's credential, or future client-supplied calendar selection), the organizer's OAuth key is used to write events into another user's calendar — cross-tenant calendar write. The lookup WHERE id=$credentialId has no userId filter, unlike this.calendarCredentials which is pre-scoped to the booking's users.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a `destination.credentialId` is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches it from the DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } ... })` with no `userId`/`teamId` scoping check, then constructs a credential object including `key` and uses it to call `createEvent(...)`. This diff therefore introduces an unscoped credential lookup by ID that could allow using (and loading secrets for) a credential not belonging to the intended booking/user/team if `destinationCalendar` can ever reference an unexpected `credentialId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateAllCalendarEvents performs the same unscoped prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } }) with no ownership scoping on the fetched credential. Same cross-tenant exposure as the create path: an unscoped reference.credentialId causes the fetched credential's secret key to be used to update/delete events on a calendar the booking owner may not control; the query trusts the id with no userId or teamId filter.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` the updated `updateAllCalendarEvents` path now falls back to fetching a credential from the DB when it’s not found in `this.calendarCredentials`. That fallback uses `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } })` (and similarly in the new create path) with no `userId`/`teamId` ownership scoping. The code then constructs a `credential` object including `key` and uses it to `updateEvent(...)`, meaning an untrusted or cross-tenant `reference.credentialId` could cause use of another tenant’s credential secret to update/delete calendar events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleCancelBooking fetches prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) with no userId/teamId scope when the reference's credentialId is not among the booking user's credentials. A booking reference carrying a credentialId owned by a different user results in that foreign credential (including its secret key via getCalendar) being used to delete events on the other user's calendar; the fallback lookup deliberately bypasses the ownership check the user.credentials.find() filter previously enforced.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking`, when a calendar reference has `credentialId` but it is not found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, the new fallback does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then uses that returned credential in `getCalendar(calendarCredential)` to perform `deleteEvent(...)` (see added block around `foundCalendarCredential`). The diff shows no `userId`/`teamId`/booking ownership scoping on this lookup, so a reference containing another user’s `credentialId` would cause using that foreign credential to delete calendar events, bypassing the previous ownership constraint enforced by searching only in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] After the destinationCalendar fallback becomes an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` dereferences undefined and throws a TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is []. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten createAllCalendarEvents multi-destination loop, the new prisma.credential.findUnique DB fallback, and the new createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId) call have no test in this diff — the only test change is apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts line 249, which merely updates the expected serialized payload shape (destinationCalendar: []); it never exercises multiple destination calendars, the credential-from-DB fallback, or the per-credential event creation. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`: it now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` to create multiple calendar events, adds a DB fallback via `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` when a credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, and passes `destination.externalId` through `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (with `CalendarManager.createEvent` now returning `externalId`/`credentialId`). "primary"` approach (and it changes what happens in the previously-tolerated 404 mismatch scenario), but the diff contains no unit/integration test asserting which `calendarId` is used for either the match or no-match path (the only test change shown is an e2e fixture expectation from `null` to `[]`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The Meet-fallback check dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without a null guard, so destinationCalendar === null (the common case now that handleNewBooking sets it to null) throws TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Every booking without a destination calendar that selects Google Meet crashes inside EventManager with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' where the old code (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) correctly fell back to integrations:daily; booking creation 500s.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new Meet fallback logic does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this will throw `TypeError`. This is a regression vs the previous safe optional-chaining check `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. The diff also shows `handleNewBooking` can set `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one, making the crash path plausible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is tautological: it runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares each cal.externalId against undefined and always returns undefined, replacing the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback. Reschedule/update of any booking whose stored reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the Google API rejects the update (or writes to the wrong target), so reschedules silently fail to propagate to the organizer's calendar. The same tautological find is repeated in deleteEvent (lines 312-315), so deletes without externalCalendarId now target calendarId undefined instead of the destination calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` now compute the fallback calendar ID as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` in the branch that only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so the `.find(...)` comparison is effectively against `undefined` and will almost always return `undefined`, removing the previous meaningful fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This is a real regression in calendar selection logic when no `externalCalendarId` is provided, potentially causing updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar (or fail if passed through without a default).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops when evt.destinationCalendar is null, dropping all collected teamDestinationCalendars for COLLECTIVE bookings where neither the eventType nor the organizer has a destination calendar. For collective team events with no eventType-level calendar, the other members' destination calendars are collected into teamDestinationCalendars but never attached to evt, so their calendar events are silently never created while the booking API still reports success — dropped work reported as success.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`... : null`). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Because this uses optional chaining, it silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, even if `teamDestinationCalendars` was populated from other team members’ `user.destinationCalendar`. That means those member calendars are never attached to `evt`, so downstream logic that relies on `event.destinationCalendar` being a non-empty array (`createAllCalendarEvents` checks `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`) will not create events for them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, createEvent silently falls back to calendarId "primary", creating the event on the credential's primary calendar instead of the selected destination. The 404 scenario this PR was meant to fix is now masked as a silent partial success: the event lands on the wrong calendar, the booking stores the reference anyway, and subsequent updates/deletes target the wrong calendar id — with no log and no error surfaced to the user.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId;` and then unconditionally falls back to `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If no destination calendar matches the given `credentialId`, the event will be inserted into the credential’s primary calendar instead of failing (previously a mismatched `externalId` would likely 404). This is “silent” because there’s no log/error when the match is missing, and `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts` still returns/stores `externalId` (passed from `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` as `destination.externalId`) even if GoogleCalendarService actually used `primary`, creating a mismatch for later update/delete targeting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In createAllCalendarEvents, when the DB-fetched credential has no app relation (credentialFromDB.app?.slug is null), credential stays undefined and the destination is silently skipped with no log and no failure result. A booking referencing a calendar credential whose app record is missing returns success to the user while that destination calendar event is silently never created — dropped work reported as success, with zero observability.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination has `credentialId` and the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the code fetches it from DB via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})`. It only reconstructs `credential` inside `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug) { ... }`. If `credentialFromDB` exists but `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is null/undefined, `credential` remains undefined, and the subsequent `if (credential) { ... createdEvents.push(...) }` block is skipped with no logging and no failure result emitted for that destination. This makes the destination calendar event silently not created, matching the finding’s “silently skipped with zero observability” claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The spread condition was inverted: `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` now always sets the organization slug, whereas the old `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set it only when billing was disabled. With team billing enabled, organizations are created with a live slug immediately at signup instead of waiting for payment, and requestedSlug is no longer reserved in metadata — unpaying users can now claim and hold org slugs, the exact behavior the billing gate existed to prevent.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the condition for setting `organization.slug` changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips when the slug is written. This means when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, the org now gets a live `slug` immediately (previously it would not). However, the finding’s claim that `requestedSlug` is no longer reserved is not supported: `metadata` still sets `requestedSlug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true (the new ternary is equivalent to the old `&&`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when neither the in-memory credentials nor the DB fetch yield a credential, `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)` is still invoked with credential undefined. getCalendar(undefined) throws inside the loop, which is caught by the outer catch and converted into failure results for ALL calendar references — one missing credential turns every reference's update (including ones that would have succeeded) into reported failures, and the real cause (missing credential) is misreported under the generic error message.
matched_golden_ids: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue highlights that `updateEvent` is called even when no credential is found (in-memory or DB), resulting in `credential` being undefined and causing a runtime error inside `getCalendar(undefined)`. This matches the golden issue about passing an undefined credential to `updateEvent` when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The reference loop multiplies remote delete calls: for each of N calendar references, the no-credentialId branch deletes via all M calendar credentials and the recurring branch loops all updatedBookings, issuing N×M (or N×bookings) deleteEvent calls against the same uids. Users with multiple calendar references on a booking now trigger duplicate remote DELETE requests to Google/Office365 on every cancellation — amplified outbound API calls that can exhaust API quotas and produce confusing 404/410 retry noise, with no dedup or bound.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` is changed from `find(...)` to `filter(...)` and then iterated (`for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`). Inside that loop, the `!credentialId` branch now loops over *all* calendar credentials (`for (const credential of calendarCredentials) ... deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)`), so multiple `_calendar` references without `credentialId` cause duplicate remote deletes (N refs × M creds) for the same `uid/externalCalendarId` pairs. Additionally, in the `credentialId` branch, the recurring-event path maps over all calendar credentials and then loops `updatedBookings`, and this whole block is now also inside the outer references loop—multiplying deletes further when a booking has multiple calendar references. There is no dedup/bounding in the diff to prevent repeated `deleteEvent` calls against the same UID(s), so the finding about amplified outbound DELETE requests is directly supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createEvent swallows every non-404 error into `return undefined` with only a server log (and the broken-integration email disabled), so the caller cannot distinguish 'created' from 'failed' — and with multi-destination creation this PR adds, one failed destination is invisible in the returned EventResult shape beyond a boolean. With the new fan-out to multiple destination calendars, a partial failure (e.g., 2 of 3 calendars created) is indistinguishable from full success to callers storing booking references — the stored externalCalendarId/credentialId for the failed destination points at a nonexistent event, and later reschedules/deletes of that reference fail opaquely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts#createEvent` catching *all* errors from `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and returning `undefined` from the catch path (with only `log.error`, and the broken-integration email still commented out). With the new fan-out in `EventManager#createAllCalendarEvents` over `event.destinationCalendar` destinations and the new `externalId` field added to `EventResult` (and used to populate `externalCalendarId`), failures can be represented only via `success: false`/`createdEvent: undefined` rather than surfacing an error. While the finding overstates 'cannot distinguish' (there is a `success` boolean), the diff-grounded concern is that partial failures are easy to ignore and the API does not force callers to handle them, especially now that multiple destination creations are attempted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In the first result mapping, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the old fallback to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`, so when calendar creation failed (creationResult undefined), the stored booking reference has a null credentialId. Failed-or-partial calendar creations now persist references without credentialId, pushing bookings onto the legacy no-credentialId code path on later reschedule/cancel (delete-by-trying-every-credential), which this refactor was specifically trying to retire — degraded behavior for exactly the bookings that already had a calendar failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the fallback to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` in the EventManager reference mapping, but `CalendarManager.createEvent(...)` was changed to always include `credentialId: credential.id` in its returned `EventResult` (and now also `externalId`). That return object is produced even when the underlying provider call fails and `creationResult` is `undefined` (it sets `success = false` but still returns the `EventResult` with `credentialId`). Therefore, from what’s shown, failed calendar creations should still persist a non-null `credentialId` via `result.credentialId`, so the claimed regression (“references without credentialId”) is not verifiable from this diff.
